_about: Coverage registry for e2e/all-games.spec.ts and backend/tests/test_e2e_game_coverage.py.
This file is the ONLY hand-maintained list in the 'every game is playable' suite, and it is
deliberately an EXCEPTION list, never a catalog. all-games.spec.ts enumerates GET /catalog at
load time, so a new game is played automatically the moment it ships; nothing here has to be
touched for that to happen. Entries exist only where a game cannot be driven by the generic
path, and each one is a decision with a reason attached.
JSON rather than TypeScript because two languages read it: the Playwright suite (which drives
the browser) and the pytest guard (which owns the backend catalog and therefore has to be the
thing that fails when a game is added without coverage). A .ts module would leave the guard

_waiver_schema.reason: Required, >= 30 chars. WHY the suite structurally cannot drive this game.
_waiver_schema.revisit_when: Required. The condition under which this waiver should be deleted.
_waiver_schema.still_asserted: Optional. What the suite DOES still check for this game, so the waiver is not read as 'zero coverage'.

photo_clue.reason: The player leg needs a real camera: the submit step is a getUserMedia capture, and Chromium's fake video device produces a frame the image pipeline rejects, so no automated player can complete a round. SPEC-TESTING §6 records this as a permanent waiver rather than a gap.
photo_clue.revisit_when: The photo submit path accepts an uploaded file (not only a live capture) in test builds, or a deterministic fake-camera fixture lands.
photo_clue.still_asserted: play-through is waived; the catalog leg (picker tile + rules modal) and room creation still run, so a broken photo_clue catalog entry is still caught.

_plan_schema._keyed_by: Catalog game id (NOT game_type) so the four occasion bingos can each carry their own deck while sharing the bingo runtime.
_plan_schema.content: Declarative prepared-content step run before /room/create. {endpoint, body, id_field, room_field}. `body.deck_prefix` expands to a 24-item deterministic deck.
_plan_schema.room_body: Extra fields merged into the /room/create body.
_plan_schema.settle_ms: Extra wait after the game starts, before the first-screen assertion. Per-game because there is no universal 'game started' selector across 38 engines.
_plan_schema.expect_button: Accessible name of a button that only the running game renders. Stronger than the generic not-lobby/not-blank check where one exists.
_plan_schema.expect_testid: data-testid that only the running game renders.

housie._why: Quick-start defaults to caller_mode 'manual' (main.py _sanitize_housie_game). Manual is a real product mode and the caller screen renders fine, but 'auto' also proves the auto-caller loop survived deploy, which is the part that silently breaks.

bingo._why: Custom Bingo has no default deck worth asserting on; a deterministic 24-item deck makes the board reproducible.

baby_bingo._why: Occasion bingos are catalog VARIANTS: game_type is 'bingo' and /room/create rejects game_type 'baby_bingo' (correct behaviour). The variant identity lives in its deck, so each one gets its own deck here. These four are exactly the games that shipped with zero e2e coverage.

impostor._why: Pass-and-play (SPEC-PASS-AND-PLAY §2): ZERO connected players by design, seats are typed by the host. Any gate based on connected players never fires. The suite generates seat_names from config_schema.players.min, so this stays catalog-driven.
impostor._why_pass_screen: The FIRST playable screen is the pass screen ('Pass the phone to Maya' + 'I'm ready'), not the privacy gate — the gate mounts only after the first player accepts the phone. Asserting privacy-gate-shield failed against a perfectly healthy game.

drawing._why: The host screen is 'Drawer: X / Clue: ___' and the round takes a few seconds to open (see store-breadth.spec.ts).

find_someone._why: Check-in style game; the first board takes a moment to populate (store-breadth uses 6s).

musical_chairs._why: Loads audio loops before the first round screen settles.

_max_players_note: max_players is the ceiling on how many real browser contexts the suite will spin up for one
game. Mafia's minimum is 6, so 8 leaves headroom. A future game with a higher minimum than
this is genuinely un-runnable by the suite: the pytest guard fails on it and forces either a
raise here or an explicit waiver.
